data.description:
The two screens that take a freelancer from signed-out to charge-ready, built to Jonah's wireframes and states ledgers from AS-30 and consuming the AS-29 tokens (docs/design/tokens/tokens.css). Screen 1: a single auth route with sign-up and sign-in modes. Screen 2: Connect Stripe — start onboarding, and show connection status with its full states ledger (not started, incomplete requirements, pending verification, enabled, expired link, error).

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 rows C-08 (sign-up/sign-in screen) and C-12 (Connect Stripe screen); section 4.3 screens 1 and 2 of 7.

DECISION CONTEXT. Two screens are merged into one task with a written justification, which milestone plan section 8.2 permits: one reviewable claim ("a new freelancer can get from nothing to an account that can charge"), around 450 projected lines, under the split threshold. This task carries a depends_on edge to AS-30; per milestone plan section 8.1, ONLY screen-rendering tasks may. If AS-30 has not yet delivered these two screens' wireframes and states ledgers, do not improvise them — pull a non-UI task instead; the graph is built so one is always available (section 8.4).

Sign-up is deliberately email-free: no verification mail, no magic link, no password reset (row C-09, OUT — Rule 1, and independently Rule 3, since email needs an ESP account and a sender domain the unnamed product cannot have).

VERIFICATION: screens render sensibly at 375px before desktop widths (front-end design plan section 5.4, the lesson of AS-23); every visual property traces to a named token, no magic values (section 5.1); every state in the ledger is reachable in a test or at a documented URL; the flow works against the local compose stack with no accounts — Connect start is exercised against stripe-mock, and the real hosted round trip belongs to the acceptance run.

NOT IN THIS TASK: the server halves (auth and Connect tasks); an account-settings screen (row C-41, OUT — Rule 1: connection status lives on screen 2, and the freelancer's invoice branding lives in their own Stripe account, row C-14, Rule 2); password-reset or verification UI (row C-09); an onboarding checklist or guided tour (row C-55, OUT — Rule 1, with Rule 4 barring the "it builds trust" counter-argument).

data.body:
Opening the UI tier. AS-45 first of the four screens because it is the only one whose subject is reachable by a signed-out visitor, and because it discharges an obligation marker AS-40 left in routes/auth.js — renderSignIn is a stub today with an explicit AS-45 OBLIGATION comment on it.

Gate checked before pulling, since the description makes it a precondition rather than an assumption: AS-30 is done and delivered docs/design/wireframes/screen-1-signin.html, screen-2-connect-stripe.html, the states ledger and 00-flows.md, plus docs/design/tokens/tokens.css at 12 kB. Nothing needs improvising, so the description's instruction to pull a non-UI task instead does not fire.

Marcus implements, on rotation — Lena ran the last two implementation stages, including a rework — and because he built the Connect server half that screen 2 renders the states of.

Two things the planner should weigh that the earlier server tasks did not face. First, this is the first task in this app that renders HTML for a human, so AS-42's escaping discipline stops being a contract-document concern and becomes a page concern; the plan should say what the view layer's escaping guarantee is and how it is proven, not inherit an assumption. Second, the verification clause demands every visual property trace to a named token with no magic values — that is a checkable property, so it should be checked mechanically rather than by review reading.

Plan written. The view-layer decisions AS-46/47/48 inherit: (1) escaping is three lexical properties over views/ — no `<%-` anywhere, no interpolation in href/src/action/formaction/style/on* or in <script>/<style>, and data-carrying attributes double-quoted — each a dependency-policy concept row with a measured baseline (P1: 0 files; P2a: 1 occurrence today, views/scaffold.ejs:38, which is why retiring the scaffold is a precondition and not housekeeping). Raw output is gated by a counted, line-pinned allowlist landed EMPTY, so AS-47's one contract-document site is its first reviewable entry rather than a widened rule. (2) The token rule replaces assets.test.js's naive check (hex literals + includes('var(--')), which passes on a stylesheet full of px values; the new one resolves every var(--name) against the vendored tokens.css and pins declaration/reference counts before quantifying. (3) A screen is a pure view model plus a presentation-only template, and a screen's GET route joins its capability's area router, never a new mount in app.js. Two live hazards found and defused in the plan: screen 2's wireframe copy says 'money', which trips the money-representation concept row from a .ejs file (reworded to 'funds', which is Flow 2's own word), and 02-states-ledger.md's S2-ABANDON row is stale against AS-41 creating the connected-account row at start. Re-projected size is ~1,300 lines against the description's 450, so §8 carries a pre-agreed split at 900 changed lines with the seam at view-layer+screen-1 / screen-2. 30 ACs, 12 falsification recipes.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-45 on feat/AS-45-onboarding-ui, per the plan: the three lexical escaping properties as concept rows with the raw-output row landing empty, the token check that resolves every var() against the vendored tokens rather than merely counting literals, both screens with their offline-reachable states, and the two loading states recorded as unrenderable rather than untested. Retiring the scaffold view is a precondition of the attribute-interpolation guard, not housekeeping.

IMPLEMENTATION REPORT — AS-45 (developer-marcus). Branch feat/AS-45-onboarding-ui, commits 94509ac and f62e82c.

THE HEADLINE: THE PRE-AGREED SPLIT TRIGGER FIRED, AND I STOPPED. Plan §8 said to measure `git diff --stat master...feat/AS-45-onboarding-ui` at the moment screen 1 was complete and green, and to stop if it exceeded 900 changed lines. Measured at that moment: 1,505 insertions + 244 deletions = 1,749 changed lines — over the line on the total AND on insertions alone. So screen 2 is NOT in this task. I filed AS-70 "D1 v1 UI: onboarding screen 2 (Connect Stripe)" carrying §3.5.2, §3.5.3, §3.6, ACs 12-14, the money-word landmine and recipes F7/F11 verbatim, with depends_on edges to AS-45, AS-30 and AS-41; AS-69 and AS-50 now depend on it too, because both need screen 2 and neither should be startable without it. Final size after the README commit: 1,664 insertions + 270 deletions = 1,934 changed lines.

I want to be plain that this is over the plan's own projection for BOTH screens (~1,300). Where it went: the test edits were projected at ~110 and came to 394 — the four new concept rows, the wholly-replaced token check (149 lines in assets.test.js, of which the CSS named-colour list is ~17), and an auth.test.js body-assertion rework the plan did not anticipate at all (deviation 1). signin-view.js came to 219 against ~62/file. I did not trim prose to get under the line: stripping the reasoning out of a guard to beat a line count is exactly what "decided now so it is not decided under pressure" forbids, and even a ruthless strip would not have reached 900.

FILES TOUCHED (17; measured `git diff --numstat master`)
  created  lib/screens/signin-view.js       +219
  created  views/signin.ejs                 +146
  created  public/app.css                   +271
  created  test/screens.test.js             +379
  deleted  views/scaffold.ejs               -48
  deleted  public/scaffold.css              -79
  modified routes/auth.js                   +73/-19
  modified routes/pages.js                  +26/-24
  modified lib/auth/guard.js                +38/-10
  modified lib/views.js                     +14/-9
  modified lib/connect/onboarding.js        +5/-4   (comment only — the one edit §11 item 5 permits)
  modified test/assets.test.js              +140/-9
  modified test/auth.test.js                +58/-13
  modified test/dependency-policy.test.js   +129/-9
  modified test/harness.test.js             +4/-1
  modified test/health.test.js              +16/-15
  modified README.md                        +146/-30
Nothing outside plan §2's list except README.md (in §2) and lib/connect/onboarding.js (permitted by §11 item 5). docs/design/** untouched. CLAUDE.md, README.md (root), PHILOSOPHY.md, agents.md untouched.

SUITE
  Offline (`docker compose -p asc-inv-as45 run --rm --build test`): 396 tests, 378 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped, 17 test files. Baseline before I started: 381/363/0/18.
  Contract (`... run --rm --build contract`): 396 tests, 396 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. No stripe-mock case added or modified (AC 27).
  THE SKIP SET, all 18, all mock-gated by `ASC_STRIPE_MOCK_URL` and untouched by this task — the offline 18 are exactly the contract run's extra 18 passes:
    connect.test.js  M1 start / M2 return / M3 refresh against stripe-mock (3)
    invoices.test.js M1 finalize / M2 send / M3 the reconciliation guard (3)
    stripe-mock.test.js, all 12: the mock is reachable and is not Stripe; strict version check is on; connected POST /v1/customers; POST /v1/invoiceitems; POST /v1/invoices; POST /v1/invoices/{id}/finalize; POST /v1/invoices/{id}/send; GET /v1/invoices/{id}; platform POST /v1/accounts + POST /v1/account_links + GET /v1/accounts/{id}; unknown parameters are rejected by the mock; Idempotency-Key is echoed; the mock ACCEPTS the forbidden shape raw while the client refuses it.

FALSIFICATION — 12 recipes plus F2's second direction. Harness at scratchpad/mutate.py: subject is a `git archive HEAD` extract OUTSIDE the worktree, backups OUTSIDE the extract (so none can enter the build context), assert-applied on disk AND inside the built image by occurrence count (`s.split(needle).length-1`, the `grep -oF | wc -l` shape, never `grep -c`), and it ABORTS on a count mismatch rather than running the suite. Restoration proved by a sha256 manifest of all 487 extract files (drift: NONE, after every batch) plus `git status --porcelain` empty in the worktree, then rebuild-and-re-run.

  F12 before: clean exit 0, zero failures. ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 exit 1, failing exactly ['V1: the runner can fail'].
  F1  raw output on a rendered user value. applied disk 1 / image 1. predicted 2, observed 2 — MATCH: 'a value containing markup is rendered as text, not as markup' + the concept-row case.
  F2  the P1 row. applied disk 1 / image 1. predicted 1, observed 1 — MATCH.
  F2 second direction (the used-exemption half): hit + sanction + cardinality literal 0->1 => exit 0, GREEN. Then remove the hit, keep the entry => exit 1, and the message is verbatim "RAW_OUTPUT_SANCTIONED views/signin.ejs matched 0 line(s), expected 1 — the entry is stale: remove it, or restore what it sanctioned". The allowlist is genuinely counted, not decorative.
  F3  P2a. applied disk 1 / image 1. predicted 2, observed 2 — MATCH (see divergence A).
  F4a magic COLOUR. applied disk 1 / image 1. predicted 1, observed 1 — MATCH.
  F4b magic DIMENSION — the one that matters, the half the old check sailed past. applied disk 1 / image 1. predicted 1, observed 1 — MATCH, message "padding: 12px — dimensional literal". The replacement really happened.
  F5  unresolvable token name. applied 1/1. predicted 1, observed 1 — MATCH, message "app.css references custom propert(ies) that tokens.css does not declare: --color-text-primaryy".
  F6  breakpoint carve-out. applied 1/1. predicted 1, observed 1 — MATCH, message "500px does not equal --breakpoint-sm's 480px". It resolves the token, it does not read the comment.
  F8  screen route moved below the auth boundary. applied 1/1. PREDICTED 0, OBSERVED 0 — MATCH, and see finding B: the plan predicted 2 and was wrong.
  F9a max-width condition. applied 1/1. predicted 2, observed 2 — MATCH (mobile-first case + the breakpoint carve-out; both guards catch it).
  F9b min-width below the floor. applied 1/1. predicted 2, observed 2 — MATCH.
  F10 script element. applied 1/1. predicted 1, observed 1 — MATCH.
  F12 after, on a REBUILT image: exit 0, zero failures.
  Every recipe matched its prediction. Two predictions I revised BEFORE running, and why:
  DIVERGENCE A (F3): the plan predicted one case. I predicted two, because screens.test.js asserts the mode-switch form's `action` and the plan was written before that case existed. Observed two. The plan's number was stale, not the guard.
  DIVERGENCE B (F4a/F4b/F9a): as written these recipes ADD a declaration, so assets.test.js's declaration-count assertion fires FIRST and the conformance half is never reached — the recipe would have gone red for the wrong reason, which is precisely the phantom this discipline exists to catch. I made the mutation also move the committed count literal, which is exactly what a developer adding a magic value would do, so the CONFORMANCE assertion is the thing under test. Recorded rather than quietly worked around.

FINDING B — F8 FAILS TO FALSIFY ANYTHING, AND THE PLAN'S PREDICTION FOR IT IS WRONG. Moving `router.get('/signin')` out of publicAuthRoutes into sessionAuthRoutes — below the auth boundary, no other change — leaves the suite GREEN (exit 0, zero failures). The plan predicted G2 and G3 would fire. Neither can:
  * G2 and G3 derive the protected partition from the PUBLIC_ROUTES literal, not from mount position. 'GET /signin' is declared public there, so it is filtered out of the protected set no matter which router registers it.
  * Behaviourally the two positions are indistinguishable for this one path, BECAUSE of the AS-64 carve-out: `requireSession` returns `next()` for `req.path === SIGNIN_PATH` before it can redirect, so a cookieless GET reaches the handler and answers 200 either way.
  So the carve-out does not "interact with" the mount position as §3.3.2 claims — it makes the position unobservable for that path, which is arguably what it is for. The residual risk is real but narrow: screen 1's publicness is asserted by a declaration and by behaviour, and not by placement. I did NOT widen a test to close this — `discoverRoutes` cannot see which sub-router registered a route, so closing it is a real change to the walker and is out of this task's scope. Flagging it for the reviewer and the CTO to route.

THE 375px INSPECTION — WHAT I LOOKED AT, AND WHAT I DID NOT
  Method, and an instrument error worth recording: my first pass used `chrome --headless=new --window-size=375,812 --screenshot`, and a layout probe reported innerW=500 — headless Chrome IGNORED the width and I had been looking at 375px-wide CROPS of a 500px layout. Those crops showed the inputs running off the right edge and I nearly reported a defect that did not exist. The instrument was wrong, not the page. I re-rendered every state inside a 375px-wide iframe in a 600px window; the probe then read innerW=375, docScrollW=375, bodyScrollW=375, main=375, field=343 — a true 375px layout viewport and NO horizontal overflow. Every image below is from that harness.
  LOOKED AT — all four rendered ledger states, eight renders, dark scheme (headless default):
    S1-DEFAULT-SIGNIN — clean; fields, button and the mode-switch control all inside the measure.
    S1-DEFAULT-SIGNIN with ?next= — the "Sign in to continue." reason line renders above the form, correctly subordinate to the h1.
    S1-DEFAULT-SIGNUP — three fields, no reset-flow hint (that span is `data-wf-note` in the wireframe, so it is annotation and deliberately not built).
    S1-ERROR-VALIDATION, one field (bad email) — banner "1 field needs attention", the email field marked, its message under it, name preserved.
    S1-ERROR-VALIDATION, two fields (both blank) — "2 fields need attention", exactly two marked.
    S1-ERROR-VALIDATION, weak password — the password field is MARKED AND EMPTY. This is Flow 6 step 2 visible on a pixel, and it is the thing I most wanted eyes on.
    S1-ERROR-SYSTEM, email taken — driven with a deliberately hostile 91-character address. THE LONG-STRING CASE THE MECHANICAL HALF CANNOT CHECK: `overflow-wrap: break-word` on `.banner` wraps it across four lines inside the banner without widening the box. This is why that declaration is there.
    S1-ERROR-SYSTEM, bad credentials — one generic sentence, the submitted email preserved, no error class and no step anywhere on the page.
  ALSO LOOKED AT — light scheme, two states: S1-DEFAULT-SIGNUP and S1-ERROR-SYSTEM(email taken). Both correct; the long address still wraps.
  DID NOT LOOK AT, and I am naming them rather than implying coverage:
    * The light scheme for the other six renders. I checked two of eight.
    * Any real device or real mobile browser. This is headless Chrome only — no iOS Safari, no Android Chrome, so the viewport-meta claim is asserted by markup and by Chrome, never by the browser the meta exists for.
    * Widths other than 375 (and, in the light pass, only those two states). No 320px, no tablet, no desktop.
    * Actual interaction: focus rings, tap-target size under a real finger, the keyboard-avoidance behaviour a mobile browser applies when a field is focused. Nothing was clicked or focused — these are static screenshots.
    * S1-LOADING: not looked at because it does not exist and cannot (no client-side JavaScript). Recorded as `unrenderable — browser-supplied`, asserted as such in screens.test.js.
    * Every screen-2 state: not built. AS-70.

LITERALS THAT MOVED (all measured, none copied from the plan)
  test/dependency-policy.test.js  app-source cardinality 49 -> 50, and the list: -2 (public/scaffold.css, views/scaffold.ejs) +3 (lib/screens/signin-view.js, public/app.css, views/signin.ejs). The plan predicted 52 for both screens; 50 is the measured truth for this scope. Concept-row test title gains AS-45.
  test/auth.test.js  ALL_ROUTES 16 -> 17 (+'GET /signin'); G1 16 -> 17; G1b 15 -> 16; G15 17 (the plan's §5 table missed G15 — deviation 2); PUBLIC_ROUTES 5 -> 6 with its reason comment. G2's protected list and G3's count stay at 11 — 'GET /signin' is public, so the protected partition did not move. G6 '/scaffold.css' -> '/app.css'.
  test/harness.test.js  EXPECTED_TEST_FILES 16 -> 17 (+screens.test.js), V2 cardinality 16 -> 17.
  test/health.test.js  VIEWS.length stays 1 (one screen shipped, not two); VIEWS.map(v=>v.file) ['scaffold.ejs'] -> ['signin.ejs']; the broken-template fixture and its detail match scaffold -> signin.
  test/assets.test.js  PUBLIC_FILES ['scaffold.css'] -> ['app.css']; case title -> 'every visual value in public/ CSS traces to a token that exists'; three NEW committed literals, each measured at the moment app.css was finished: TOKEN_NAMES = 127 (distinct names in tokens.css, smaller than the 183 declarations because blocks 2-4 re-declare the semantic names), APP_CSS_DECLARATIONS = 98, APP_CSS_VAR_REFERENCES = 76.
  THE NOT-MOVING SET HELD, checked mechanically rather than asserted: SCHEMA.length 11; LOCK_ENTRIES 70; DIRECT_DEPENDENCIES ['ejs','express']; express 5.2.1; ejs 6.0.1; SANCTIONED.length 3; TOKENS_BYTES 12199; TOKENS_DECLARATIONS 183; SIGNIN_PATH '/signin'; POST_SIGNIN_LANDING '/'. All seven existing concept-row allowlists ('money representation', 'raw SQL', 'body parser', 'platform Stripe call', 'current user', 'contract HTML escape', 'console output') are BYTE-IDENTICAL — the diff contains no +/- line touching any of them; no view, view model or route joined any. test/connect.test.js NOT MODIFIED AT ALL (0 lines), so the §1 scope boundary was never crossed. Dockerfile, compose.yaml, package.json, package-lock.json, app.js, lib/config.js and the ten other test files all unchanged. No new dependency.

DEVIATIONS, numbered
  1. auth.test.js's H5, H6, H8 and H11 assert on RESPONSE BODIES, and discharging the renderSignIn seam necessarily changes those bodies from one-line text/plain to a rendered page. Plan §5 listed auth.test.js as "route-surface literals" only and did not anticipate this. Smallest change that keeps each case's own claim: H5 and H6 now assert the state sentinel and, for H6, the specific field message each step maps to — strictly STRONGER than the old body match, since it still distinguishes the three steps and additionally checks the words a freelancer reads. H8's byte-identity claim is preserved by masking EACH response's OWN submitted address before comparing: the two cases must submit different addresses, and what the enumeration property actually claims is that nothing else differs. H11's control moved from 200 to 303-to-/connect-stripe because `/` is a redirect now.
  2. G15 in auth.test.js carries a route-count literal (16) that plan §5's table omitted. Moved to 17.
  3. `POST_SIGNIN_LANDING` unchanged at '/', per §3.3.4 — so S1-DENIED-AUTHENTICATED 303s to '/', which routes/pages.js 303s on to /connect-stripe. Two hops until AS-48. Deliberate.
  4. The wireframe's inline "Sign in instead" ANCHOR inside the email-taken banner is rendered as plain text. An anchor cannot carry `next` without putting it in a URL position, which P2a forbids without exception; the equivalent control is the mode-switch button directly below the form. The sentence is otherwise the wireframe's, verbatim.
  5. Copy the wireframe does not supply: `missing-field` renders "This field is required." (the wireframe illustrates only the two named messages), the unmapped/parse-body system error renders "Something went wrong. Try again.", and a zero-marked-field validation banner would read "Check your details and try again." All three are renderer constants; none is ever an error message.
  6. The S1-ERROR-SYSTEM h2 stays the mode's own title. The wireframe's "Sign-up / sign-in — account errors" heading is an artifact of that document rendering both variants on one page; the banner carries the error.
  7. `'ada@example'` — the wireframe's illustration for a malformed address — is ACCEPTED by lib/auth/accounts.js (a dotless domain is legal). screens.test.js uses `'ada-at-example'`, a spelling the server really rejects. Measured, not assumed; the comment in the test says so.
  8. The plan calls the link-styled control `.link-button`; wireframe.css actually defines `.btn-link`. I used the spec's real class name.
  9. The locals object returned by signinLocals is deliberately NOT frozen: express's res.render adds `_locals` and throws "Cannot add property _locals, object is not extensible" on a frozen object. Measured, and the reason is in the code. The nested banner and both exported lists ARE frozen.
  10. lib/views.js's `sampleLocals` is now `signinLocals()` — the screen's own view model — rather than a hand-written object, so a template that grows a required local cannot drift from its health-check probe. That replaces an instruction ("add it here in the same commit") that was asking a human to remember.
  11. The plan named FIVE `AS-45 OBLIGATION` markers; there were SIX (views/scaffold.ejs carried one too, and is deleted). All are gone: `grep -rn 'AS-45 OBLIGATION\|AS-45 obligation'` now returns nothing outside .lattice/. The three files that record the discharge deliberately do NOT spell the marker phrase, or AC 24's grep would always find its own epitaph.
  12. Screen 1's route joining publicAuthRoutes means G2/G3's protected count stays 11, not the 12 plan §3.3.5 projected — that projection assumed both screens landed and 'GET /connect-stripe' is screen 2's.

LEFT UNDONE
  * Screen 2 in its entirety, and with it ACs 12, 13, 14, and recipes F7 and F11 — AS-70.
  * The `S2-ABANDON` ledger amendment (§9 Q3): routed to Jonah as a documentation follow-up, wording carried verbatim in AS-70's description. I did not edit docs/design/**.
  * Finding B above: F8 falsifies nothing, and the plan's §3.3.2 claim that the carve-out and the mount position "interact" is not true as stated. Not fixed here — closing it means changing the route walker.
  * Light-scheme and real-device visual coverage, per the DID NOT LOOK AT list.

DOCKER HYGIENE: own project names throughout (`asc-inv-as45`, `asc-inv-as45m`), the browser stack on 127.0.0.1:8353 (measured free first), never 8348 or 8347. Both protected containers verified still Up and healthy afterwards, and asc-invoicing-web-1's /healthz still answers ok:true. Both projects torn down with `down -v --remove-orphans`; all four images I built removed; no global prune; stripe/stripe-mock:v0.203.0 left pulled. `test` still `network_mode: none` — unchanged.

WHERE THE REVIEWER SHOULD START: (1) the split decision and whether AS-70's scope carve is right; (2) finding B — F8's zero-case result and what, if anything, should own it; (3) deviation 1, the auth.test.js body assertions, which is the one place I changed another task's committed assertions and the one place the plan gave no cover; (4) deviation 9, the unfrozen locals, since it is a real constraint the plan's "pure view model" framing did not anticipate.

Orchestrator rulings before review.

THE SPLIT IS UPHELD. Measured 1,749 changed lines at the screen-1-complete-and-green checkpoint against a 900-line pre-agreed trigger, and the implementer stopped rather than finishing screen 2 and reporting the overage afterwards. That is the first time a split line has actually been used to change what shipped rather than being ruled around at merge, and it is the right outcome: the trigger exists so the decision is not taken under the pressure of nearly-done work. Final scope 1,934 changed lines across 17 files. Screen 2 is AS-70, carrying the sections, criteria, the money-word landmine and the two recipes verbatim, with AS-69 and AS-50 re-pointed at it.

Verified independently: test/connect.test.js is not in the branch diff at all, docs/design/ is untouched, and views/ and public/ each contain exactly one file — the scaffold is retired, which the attribute-interpolation guard required as a precondition rather than as tidying.

His line about not trimming prose to beat the number is the part worth keeping: gaming a trigger is worse than crossing it, because a trigger that can be gamed stops measuring anything.

F8 DOES NOT FALSIFY, AND THE PLAN'S CLAIM IS WRONG — tech-lead item, not a rework trigger. Moving the sign-in route below the auth boundary leaves the suite green. The reason is that the partition tests derive their route sets from a committed literal rather than from mount position, and the guard's sign-in carve-out makes the two positions behaviourally identical for that path. So section 3.3.2's claim that carve-out and mount position interact is false as stated: the carve-out makes position UNOBSERVABLE. The implementer declined to widen a test to close it, correctly — closing it means changing the route walker, which is a design change and not his to make mid-stage. Owen should either rewrite the recipe against what is actually observable or change the walker, and say which.

DEVIATION 1 IS A PLAN GAP: discharging the render seam necessarily changes response bodies that four existing cases assert on, and section 5 gave no cover for it. He preserved the byte-identity case by masking each response's own submitted address, which keeps the property the case exists for.

THE INSTRUMENT ERROR IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THE REPORT, and it nearly produced a false defect. His first responsive pass ran headless Chrome with a 375px window flag; a layout probe read 500px, so Chrome had ignored the flag and he was inspecting crops of a 500px layout that showed inputs running off the edge. He caught it by probing the viewport instead of trusting the flag, re-rendered inside a 375px iframe, and measured no overflow. A screenshot is not evidence of the width you asked for unless something measured the width you got — and the failure mode here was a plausible-looking defect report, not a missed one.

His visual-inspection list is honest in the way the plan asked for: eight rendered states looked at in dark scheme including a deliberately hostile 91-character email, two of eight in light, and an explicit not-looked-at list covering the other six light renders, every width but 375, any real device or mobile browser, and focus and tap targets. The viewport-meta claim is therefore asserted by Chrome and never by the browser it exists for, which he says plainly.

REVIEW: assigning agent:qa-priya. Marcus implemented, so implementer != reviewer holds. Priya over Ruben on rotation — he took AS-65's two cycles — and because the first screen task's reviewable surface is a rendering guarantee, which is the shape she attacked hardest on AS-42 with 114 hostile documents.
